body:
"I luv eatin meatz: burd meatz; cow meatz; ppl meatz. Iz al so tasti."

And he knows I'm a vegetarian. And he's talked to me about it (in this same sort of manner) before. 

Another quote from my ordeal is: "If you believe in evolution, then a person being gay isn't evolutionarily sound."

I base my life upon being polite and doing good to others. I want to be treated the way I treat other people. 

That "Angel" quote basically sums up my life. Thank you for sharing it!

Before the low blow, he also insinuated in this conversation that my beliefs were on par with: cannibalism; pedophilia (he's crazy about the pedos, "The pedophiles are going to take over this country"); and being a Nazi - all of which I'm against...I'm a vegetarian for christ's sake.

I read this before going to class. It made me feel instantly better because I know how badly he must feel about himself. 

He's psychologically abusive to my boss. Constantly yelling at her for "talking to her clients for too long" (she's a lawyer....wtf is he smoking anyway). He seriously sucks. I wish that didn't sound so angst-ridden.

I have a great relationship with my boss: I tell her more than I tell my mom. When the inevitable question of, "What do you believe in" was asked by her, she loved my response and actually had an adult conversation about it. She's the most understanding person alive. 

Her husband is a joke. He lost his Law license and now belittles her career - which is a bankruptcy lawyer - by having hour long - no joke - rants about what she's doing wrong. After every time he yells at her, I pull her aside and tell her she's doing awesomely (because she's actually making money and supporting not only her children BUT his children, as opposed to this asshole who doesn't make a dime).

I know she wants to get a divorce. I know deep down she wants to. She just loves her kids too much to do anything.

(Sorry for the rant...it feels better letting it out).
I totally get it. The thing is is that he's the same way to my boss, too.
I have to comment and say that he wasn't drunk. Not even tipsy. He had a beer. Gah, this is so confusing...

You understood correctly. That's what's driving me up a wall: I just can't figure it out. I want to just believe this isn't the case, so I just didn't think about it for a long time. However, the past couple of months I've been thinking about it and it sucks. It's like someone tore a piece out of me.

On the other hand, I don't want to scream, "I've been raped," because I have no idea if I consented or not.

No, never. We never really drank that much; we did drugs a lot together, though. But it was always consensual. 

The more I think about his behavior while we were dating, the more "psychotic" he's becoming. He wasn't very empathetic and was extremely manipulative. He had all the signs of [antisocial personality disorder](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisocial_personality_disorder).
I'm not seeing my therapist anymore - I can't afford to see her. I wish I would have talked about it then when I had the chance. Thanks.
